approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a population of at most 64 scored survivors, using score-quantile parent selection, connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond mutations. It constructs a fresh field of 160 valid unique products per announced batch. A Gaussian process fitted to every accepted session observation uses count-Morgan fingerprints and a generalized Tanimoto covariance; correlated posterior draws buy ten products, with purchases restricted to the forty highest predicted means after three non-improving batches. Ordinary mutation walks and crossover finishing can take several transformations, but only their final products reach the selector, and intermediate prefixes have no persistent return statistics. Accepted offspring compete greedily for breeder membership. The latest Parent removed an escalation rule that never fired, leaving its measured trajectories unchanged.
approach.novelty: Replace that scored-population and global-predictor controller with persistent graph-prefix tree search. Keep valid unscored intermediate graphs, use every observed terminal return to update the exact path that produced it, and let those path values choose subsequent expansions and oracle purchases directly. Counts of leaves awaiting feedback discourage redundant batch exploration without inventing rewards. This tests whether a useful sequence can be learned without first scoring and retaining every intermediate. There are no completed siblings of the current Parent in the supplied brief. Earlier lineage experiments changed walk-length probabilities, diversity among scored breeders or the supply presented to the global predictor; none implemented persistent prefix-specific terminal credit with direct tree-controlled purchases.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is loss of trajectory-specific credit: the actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de discards unscored intermediate graph states and restarts fresh breeding from scored survivors, so its feedback cannot favor a previously useful unscored prefix. Its three summary.json files and run.log files show complete execution, macro 0.607030316211131 with seed standard deviation 0.030175277546149237, 4,350 accepted optimizer evaluations and no invalid/duplicate proposals. This is not an execution repair. The Parent's exact-reproduction result against n-61b9b3bfb40d locates no new search capability in the removed dormant rule. Related evidence makes a specific new credit unit testable: n-0a7915ec6f8d had positive parent-beat credit in only 399 of 2,793 credited products and a single positive-credit arm in 128 of 266 updated batches; its summed walk-length credit steered the measured task preferences in the wrong direction. n-e1a97c9e8713 increased reachable breeding skeletons from 19.05 to 29.20 yet decreased realized incumbent-increment mass from 5.978073 to 5.269884. n-c415372c2c82 changed 433 of 435 purchase sets but reduced scaffold coverage and the endpoint mean. These are counterexamples to those specific interventions, not proof that tree search works. They motivate replacing the feedback unit and purchase controller rather than retuning a length law or retaining more scored diversity.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the exact frozen w4-graph-search-controller-review (the on-disk record was checked equal to the ticket copy), including its recorded actual search queries. This plan opened the official molecular MCTS code and WU-UCT paper to verify terminal backup and the pending-count formula. PMC and HAL returned browser challenges in this read; their findings are reused from the frozen review, not claimed as newly retrieved full text. Adopt persistent molecular tree state, terminal-return backup, action progressive widening and pending-only exploration adjustment. Adapt them to inherited graph edits, fixed supplied roots, path-local credit, bounded synchronous oracle batches and session-local all-return normalization. The literature supplies no score forecast or calibrated constants for this budget. The Parent and specific credit/diversity counterexamples supply the reason for this joint replacement; no new model, package, corpus or preparation is needed.

method_change.previous_method: Actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de: score-quantile graph evolution with greedy-64 survival, a full accepted archive training a count-Tanimoto GP, fresh 160-member candidate fields, correlated Thompson purchases and stall-conditioned top-forty eligibility.
method_change.proposed_method: Persistent molecular graph-prefix MCTS forest initialized from supplied accepted molecules, observed-return UCT with action progressive widening, exact-path all-return backup, pending-aware batched leaf selection and direct oracle submission.
method_change.rationale: The code Parent contains no persistent unscored graph prefix or prefix-conditioned return estimate. Its discarded intermediates and scored survival gate cannot express the proposed mechanism. The frozen ticket therefore replaces the coordinated breeder, survival and purchase controller together while preserving graph primitives, canonical admission, source-relative sulfur admission, the accepted archive and protocol. The n-0a7915ec6f8d sparse aggregate credit and n-e1a97c9e8713 diversity-without-progress counterexamples motivate the new credit unit. Removing the useful existing predictor and evolutionary concentration is a substantive performance risk, not a free simplification. Only the joint replacement is identified by this experiment.

hypothesis: One joint replacement: persistent prefix-conditioned, all-observed-terminal-return MCTS with progressive action widening and WU-UCT-style pending-aware direct batch selection. Prefix occurrences retain molecular states and route-specific completed counts N, observed return sums W, and pending counts O across observe boundaries. Actual terminal rewards, including non-improving and low returns, are backed up exactly once on their recorded route. UCT uses W/N only from completed observations and N+O only in its exploration term. The selected forest itself emits the announced batch of distinct valid terminal molecules, exposing tree feedback without the old GP or stall mask. The causal prediction is that real terminal feedback changes subsequent existing-prefix choices, revisits unscored intermediates, and delivers useful evaluated descendants through those intermediates; those descendants may increase realized incumbent progress and the full-panel endpoint.

finding_summary.headline: Persistent prefix credit worked, but useful progress and final scores fell sharply
finding_summary.insights: Loss of prefix memory, positive-only credit and an intervening GP filter do not explain this run: persistent memory, all-return feedback and direct purchases all operated. The limitation is how the activated method uses its limited feedback. Of 13,049 non-root occurrences, 10,584 finished with only one terminal return; 2,299 of the 2,681 feedback-sensitive decisions were still choices among the ten original roots. Real deeper reuse occurred, but it did not sustain useful refinement: late-half evaluations produced 12 incumbent improvements versus the Parent’s 76. Chemistry supports diffuse exploration rather than scaffold collapse: typed/generic scaffold counts rose from 1,667/951 to 2,718/2,085 and fragment-excluded similarity fell on every task, while scaffold coverage fell and both tiny and oversized tails expanded from 91/44 to 350/472. Favorable combinations of rings and polar functionality were reachable but less consistently preserved; broader scaffold variety alone did not solve the search problem. A proposal or ranking model that generalizes feedback across related graph states and preserves useful local arrangements is the kind of method that could address this sparse, weakly focused refinement; this run does not test such a method. The literature-derived persistence, backup, pending accounting and widening elements all operated in their registered molecular adaptations, so this is an informative failure of their bound conversion prediction. Because the replacement also removed the Parent’s predictor and scored breeding concentration, the evidence identifies a negative result for the joint controller and cannot isolate the contribution of tree credit, widening, pending accounting or the removed components. It leaves broader tree-search approaches open and supplies no counterfactual scores for unchosen routes.
finding_summary.results: All 15 sessions completed. The tree delivered 3,044 of 4,350 evaluated proposals through 2,296 intermediate occurrences retained unscored across batches. Every accepted return was backed up correctly, including 4,302 non-improving returns. Freezing values at their pre-feedback level changed 2,681 actual choices, including 382 below the root selector; pending counts changed 3,930 same-state selections. Retained-prefix descendants produced 24 incumbent improvements totaling 0.6483. Yet full-panel improvement mass fell from 5.9781 to 1.4670, or from 0.00137427 to 0.000337234 per evaluation, triggering the registered useful-progress falsifier. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.306290 (paired difference −0.300740, against a required +0.002). All three seed macros and all five task means fell; 14 of 15 endpoints were lower, and every task mean exceeded its allowed regression margin. These results establish activation and refute this intervention’s predicted conversion to better search.

molecular.headline: Broad aromatic and heterocyclic chemistry with expanded fragment and oversized tails, reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of Algorithm Node n-eca1b7eb5895 against code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, confined to the frozen Search panel: five tasks, seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations per session including ten supplied initial records. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true. All fifteen Child paths in context.citation_trajectory_paths and all fifteen published Parent paths in focus.artifacts.parent_trajectories were read in full; none is missing. Each arm contains 4,500 accepted records, of which 4,350 are optimizer proposals. All 4,350 proposals per arm parse as connected RDKit molecules. No heldout or Confirmation evidence was read. Parent history was checked through context.evidence_index.node_path_template for n-cf8d309c06de, but current Parent comparisons below were independently recomputed from its published Search trajectories, not copied from its truncated digest. Parent-only SMILES are not quoted in cited_smiles, because the trusted citation list in this request covers the Child trajectories. Population readings use RDKit 2023.09.6, optimizer rows only, without deduplicating evaluations. Sizes are heavy-atom counts; tails mean strictly below six and above fifty. Ring counts use RDKit's symmetry-perceived ring set, so cage ring counts are representation diagnostics rather than independent ring-building steps. Typed scaffolds are canonical nonempty Murcko scaffolds, generic scaffolds use MakeScaffoldGeneric, and coverage is the fraction of all proposals with a nonempty scaffold. Similarities are all unordered RDKit sparse-count Morgan-radius-two Tanimoto pairs within each task pooled across seeds after excluding molecules below six heavy atoms; exactly the same definitions are applied to Parent. Top/bottom deciles mean 87 of 870 optimizer rows per task, with stable trajectory order resolving score ties; these are descriptive score strata, not new scores or molecule selections. Both per-seed 29-row deciles and chronological halves were also inspected. The output comprises phenyl and aza-aromatic systems, oxygenated heterocycles, pyrazoline/imine/thione chemistry, amides, cyclic amines, esters, acids, ethers and fused dicarbonyl N-heterocycles, along with fragmented remnants and very large combinations of those motifs. It has broad scaffold variety, rather than one collapsed scaffold family: global nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts rise from Parent 1,667/951 to Child 2,718/2,085. Nevertheless coverage falls from 4,255/4,350 to 3,816/4,350, and global canonical unique molecules fall from 4,304 to 4,136 because exact molecules recur across independent sessions; within-task uniqueness remains 851-862 of 870. The global heavy-atom median stays 28, concealing simultaneous tail expansion: Parent below-six/above-fifty counts 91/44 become 350/472. Both tails are larger in every matched task/seed cell, and both remain present in every Child session's last 145 proposals. Global Child mean rings/aromatic rings are 3.41/2.07 versus Parent 3.92/2.62, so expanded scaffold coverage in identity space does not imply more rings per molecule. In the fixed task order, fragment-excluded mean pair similarity is Child 0.13263, 0.13079, 0.13237, 0.13646, 0.12306 versus Parent 0.30059, 0.20433, 0.24270, 0.30356, 0.27897. Corresponding Child retained population/pair denominators are 813/330078, 786/308505, 809/326836, 802/321201 and 790/311655; Parent denominators are 850/360825, 847/358281, 850/360825, 859/368511 and 853/363378. Distinct nonempty typed scaffolds in the upper score deciles are Child 81, 78, 81, 79, 70 versus Parent 12, 12, 20, 42, 21. These data support broad output diversity without establishing a beneficial mechanism or biological utility. The quality limitations change rather than disappear. Whole-population motif-positive molecule counts, Parent to Child, are N-halogen 888 to 143, O-halogen 162 to 201, O-O bonds 118 to 287, neutral N=O matches 242 to 11, and perceived rings of at most four atoms whose atoms are all aromatic 170 to 46. Those motifs are flags for chemical review, not measured instability, toxicity or universal synthetic impossibility. Amides occur in 1,554 Child proposals, sulfonamides in 319 and nitriles in 328: those functional-group classes are demonstrably present. A deliberately limited nonaromatic amine proxy is present in 1,113 proposals, including ring-bound centers in 542; it excludes aromatic attachment and adjacency to heteroatoms or imine/carbonyl/sulfonyl environments and is not a pKa or protonation calculation. Every Child task's digest has charged_rate=0.0 and stereocentre_rate=0.0. RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,547 proposals and no assigned centers in any; their conformations, stereoselective synthesis and protonation behavior were not evaluated. Ordinary medicinal fragments coexist with reactive groups, cages and size extremes, supporting questionable synthetic plausibility and only moderate drug-like character. The score associations below describe observed molecules and cannot attribute chemistry changes to an individual controller component. Reproducible derived evidence is in policy/scratch/r0050-00-molecular/chemistry_audit.py and metrics.json; the authority for citations remains the immutable request and its trusted paths.

per_task.generated_character: Full proposal population: 870 accepted optimizer molecules across seeds 0/1/2, all parsed. Heavy atoms span 1-108 (median 27); mean molecular weight 416.5 Da; mean perceived rings/aromatic rings 3.46/2.15. Below-six/above-fifty heavy-atom counts are 57/102, compared with Parent 20/0. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 613/486 versus Parent 186/69; nonempty scaffold coverage is 782/870 versus 849/870. Digest ring/aromatic-string rates are 0.8989/0.7885; the aromatic rate is the fraction of strings containing aromatic atom tokens, not an aromatic atom fraction. The center of the population contains substituted aromatic/heteroaromatic systems bearing amides, ethers, imines, thiones and ester or acid fragments. The highest observed optimizer molecule is a 25-heavy-atom fused pyrazoline-containing system with an N-acylthiourea unit and chloromethyl substituent (seed 0/evaluation 203); it has four perceived rings, two aromatic rings and two unassigned centers. The next example is a 25-heavy-atom acetanilide/ether-linked fused aza-ring system (seed 0/evaluation 71), a more conventional medicinal combination. A representative middle-score proposal is a 34-heavy-atom hydroperoxide-bearing conjugated chain attached to a coumarin-like aromatic system (seed 2/evaluation 67). Much larger polyaromatic combinations and tiny fragments are both common enough that the leaders do not describe the whole population. Synthetic plausibility varies: ordinary amide/ether coupling patterns are present, whereas the fused leader and peroxide chains require additional feasibility review.
liabilities: The full population includes 75 O-O, 43 N-halogen and 48 O-halogen containing molecules, plus four molecules flagged for an all-aromatic perceived ring of at most four atoms. These categories overlap.

The leader's chloromethyl substituent, thiourea-like linkage and fused stereogenic ring system raise reactivity and synthesis questions; no synthetic route or three-dimensional feasibility was demonstrated.
Both tiny fragments and large hybrids persist late in evaluation, while the final proposed molecule can have score zero despite earlier high-scoring molecules.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of compact aromatic/heterocyclic and carbonyl arrangements across the population is lacking: the upper-decile size range is 19-29 heavy atoms, yet 102 proposals exceed fifty. These motifs are reachable; sustained coherent representation is the gap.
Configurational definition is absent even in the fused, stereogenic leader. The score data do not show whether specifying stereochemistry would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The upper versus lower optimizer deciles have median heavy-atom counts 24 versus 62; the same compact-versus-large direction occurs in every seed's deciles. Seed 0/evaluation 203 scores 0.450338612, seed 0/evaluation 71 scores 0.429416835, and seed 2/evaluation 273's compact diaryl fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.412681984. By comparison, the hydroperoxide chain at seed 2/evaluation 67 scores 0.0000690361, and the late large peroxide-linked polyaromatic hybrid at seed 2/evaluation 300 scores 0.0. The gradient associates compact, structured heterocyclic/aromatic arrangements with higher values, not simply more rings or more atoms. The Parent's upper decile is also compact (median 25 heavy atoms), but much more scaffold-concentrated. This does not establish a particular target pharmacophore or make the chloromethyl/thione leader an experimentally desirable compound.

A peroxycarboxylic-acid-bearing fused dicarbonyl proposal at seed 2/evaluation 152 scores 0.159021248; a high-scoring acylated N-O/carbamoyl-bromide structure at seed 0/evaluation 62 scores 0.164987286. Familiar ring fragments can carry reactive terminal groups without a very low score.
Sixty-eight below-six-heavy-atom proposals and seventy-nine above-fifty proposals expand the size extremes even while the favorable size region remains moderate.
missing_features: Consistent preservation and refinement of the linked aza-aromatic/cyclic-carbonyl arrangements is lacking across the output, although both starting molecules and new proposals show them. Reaching more scaffolds is not evidence of preserving their relevant connectivity.

Practical three-dimensional and stereochemical definition of dense polycycles is missing; the highest new structure contains multiple unassigned centers, and no conformational or synthetic feasibility evidence is available.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The upper/lower optimizer deciles have median heavy-atom counts 33/3 and mean ring counts 4.56/0.00, consistently larger and ring-rich at the upper end in every seed. The cage leader scores 0.171546028; the piperidine amide scores 0.166644625; the diaryl/pyrrolyl dicarbonyl heterocycle at seed 0/evaluation 224 scores 0.165294901. Ethylene glycol at seed 1/evaluation 300 scores zero. A supplied initial dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.167838659, above the best newly proposed values in seeds 0 and 2, so ring variety alone has not delivered stronger versions of that initial favorable arrangement in those sessions. The Parent upper decile has median thirty heavy atoms and recurrent connected aza-aromatic/cyclic dicarbonyl chemistry. The Child samples these classes, but the observed gradient favors their complete ring/carbonyl arrangements over fragments; it does not establish that more cage bonds or reactive modifications are beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: Full proposal population: 870 accepted optimizer molecules across seeds 0/1/2, all parsed. Heavy atoms span 1-120 (median 27); mean molecular weight 410.9 Da; mean perceived rings/aromatic rings 3.23/1.88. Below-six/above-fifty heavy-atom counts are 80/91, compared with Parent 17/0. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 567/461 versus Parent 274/101; nonempty scaffold coverage is 749/870 versus 853/870. Digest ring/aromatic-string rates are 0.8609/0.7264; the aromatic rate is the fraction of strings containing aromatic atom tokens, not an aromatic atom fraction. The population is chemically diverse but has a very low observed score bulk. Higher examples are compact N-rich heterocycles: a 23-heavy-atom brominated methoxy-pyrazoline fused to an imine/thioamide-containing polycycle (seed 2/evaluation 244), a 22-heavy-atom N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine carboxamide attached to dichloropyridine (seed 1/evaluation 232), and a 23-heavy-atom fused amidine/carbonyl heterocycle with hydroxymethyl and phenyl groups (seed 0/evaluation 226). These are not a single shared scaffold. Large low-score molecules combine long unsaturated chains, multiple carbonyl/ester units, polyaryl groups and oxygenated saturated rings; some include N-O or O-O links. A middle-score example is a rigid polyaromatic nitrile with O-F connectivity, not a compact balanced member of the higher stratum. The sulfonyl carboxamide is a familiar synthetic motif, whereas the brominated fused thione system has unassigned stereochemistry and a more demanding feasibility question.
liabilities: Forty-six proposals contain O-O bonds, twenty-one N-halogen bonds and forty-two O-halogen bonds; five are flagged for very small all-aromatic perceived rings.

The 91 above-fifty-heavy-atom hybrids include elaborate unsaturation, N-O links and multiple inherited fragments, while eighty proposals have fewer than six heavy atoms. Both extremes persist through the late budget.

A late peroxycarboxylic-acid ester/aryl hybrid at seed 2/evaluation 299 scores 1.55631122e-27. Parsing, functional-group richness and aromaticity alone do not establish a favorable or practical structure.
missing_features: Repeated production of compact, coherently arranged polar N-heterocyclic molecules is underrepresented: several such structures are accessible, yet most proposals remain far from their observed score region.

A common necessary pharmacophore cannot be identified from the structurally different leaders. What is missing is stable coverage of favorable size/connectivity combinations, rather than an evidenced requirement for one named substituent or more amines.
The stereogenic fused leader and pyrrolidine carboxamide lack assigned configurations; the trajectories do not test whether configuration would alter this score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three compact examples score 0.240000227, 0.209065023 and 0.198839455. The upper/lower optimizer deciles have median heavy-atom counts 23/58, and the compact upper-end direction occurs in every seed. The large hybrid at seed 0/evaluation 298 scores zero; the middle-score O-F polyaromatic structure scores 4.05562316e-14. The full optimizer median is 3.77505908e-14; the digest's rounded median 0.0 should not be interpreted as every median-region observation being exactly zero. The favorable stratum associates moderate size and selective N-rich/polar ring arrangements with higher values, not maximized aromaticity, molecular size or aliphatic amine count: the amine proxy occurs in only 10/87 upper versus 39/87 lower proposals. The Parent's upper stratum is also compact (median 27 heavy atoms), but is enriched in different multiply halogenated heterocyclic arrangements. Its higher scores do not make those reactive motifs a transferable chemical target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-eca1b7eb5895 versus published n-cf8d309c06de, fixed Search seeds 0/1/2, five sessions per seed, 300 observations including ten initial molecules, batch ten; optimizer proposals only. Full-population below-six/above-fifty heavy-atom counts increase from 91/44 to 350/472, and both counts increase in every matched session. Both tails remain present in each Child session's late half. In two score surfaces the upper decile has median 24 or 23 heavy atoms while the lower decile has median 62 or 58; a different surface rewards larger aromatic structures. These are observed molecular associations, not component attribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted distribution lacks two-sided size discipline: tiny remnants and oversized combinations proliferate together while the median size barely changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically coherent growth and contraction that preserve useful local groups, and track both tails alongside session-local observed returns. A blanket drive toward smaller molecules or a universal hard cutoff is not supported: the observed favorable size region varies. Test whether the generator can explore distinct size bands without fragmenting or indiscriminately concatenating them; no objective identity is needed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-eca1b7eb5895 versus published n-cf8d309c06de, fixed Search seeds 0/1/2, five sessions per seed, 300 observations including ten initial molecules, batch ten; optimizer proposals only. Child proposals include 287 O-O, 201 O-halogen and 143 N-halogen positive molecules, plus 46 with a perceived all-aromatic ring of at most four atoms. Parent counts are 118, 162, 888 and 170 respectively, so this is a changed liability mixture, not a universal worsening. A carbamoyl bromide scores 0.104731845 and a peroxycarboxylic-acid-containing heterocycle scores 0.159021248 in their respective observed sessions. Neither score establishes stability or makeability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks reliable control of bond-context plausibility; reactive heteroatom linkages and demanding ring closures remain embedded in otherwise familiar scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give transformations a general, auditable vocabulary for the local bond environments they create, including O-O, heteroatom-halogen, acyl-halide and highly constrained ring connections. Provide plausible alternative attachment and ring-edit outcomes. Evaluate any change through ordinary session-local feedback; motif flags are chemical review hypotheses rather than hidden objective rewards or automatic toxicity labels.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-eca1b7eb5895 versus published n-cf8d309c06de, fixed Search seeds 0/1/2, five sessions per seed, 300 observations including ten initial molecules, batch ten; optimizer proposals only. Every task digest has stereocentre_rate=0.0 and charged_rate=0.0. Structural perception finds unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,547 of 4,350 Child proposals and no assigned centers; one cited leading cage has five unassigned centers. A nonaromatic amine proxy is present in 1,113 proposals, including ring-bound centers in 542. This proves missing explicit representation, not lack of basic atoms or a measured protonation error.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated molecules do not express defined stereochemical configurations or charged states despite frequently containing stereogenic and potentially ionizable structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make configuration and chemically consistent ionization/tautomer alternatives representable where the benchmark contract permits, with clear identity and duplicate handling. Do not presume score benefit, enumerate unbounded microstates or assert that neutral strings lack basicity; this evidence cannot establish how the evaluator treats those alternatives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-eca1b7eb5895 versus published n-cf8d309c06de, fixed Search seeds 0/1/2, five sessions per seed, 300 observations including ten initial molecules, batch ten; optimizer proposals only. Global nonempty typed/generic scaffold identities increase from 1,667/951 to 2,718/2,085 and fragment-excluded pair similarity decreases on every score surface, while nonempty scaffold coverage falls from 4,255/4,350 to 3,816/4,350. The proposal set demonstrably contains 1,554 amide, 319 sulfonamide and 328 nitrile positive molecules. On one surface a nonaromatic amine proxy occurs in 51/87 upper versus 9/87 lower proposals, yet on another it occurs in 10/87 upper versus 39/87 lower proposals. Therefore neither more diversity nor more of one functional group is a universal missing ingredient.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold exploration does not reliably preserve coherent combinations of ring geometry and polar functionality that the generator already reaches.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support alternative local edits that retain an observed useful arrangement while exploring different surrounding scaffolds, and measure chemical-family coverage and within-family improvement separately using only current-session observations. Treat the present motifs as evidence of capability and conditional combinations, not a task-specific answer or proof that a controller component caused the chemistry.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
